- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.3) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for high sentiment periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative — add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment <0.1 or near zero.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak if sentiment remains neutral or declines.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts — dampen forecast volatility if sentiment is volatile or erratic.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment peaks 2–3 days before forecast horizon, model should anticipate downward correction — reduce forecast by 1–2% for each lagged sentiment peak.
